topic.title: Accounts: connect everything Command Centre uses
topic.shortdesc: Sign in to Claude, Odoo, your mailboxes, Google and social accounts from one page. Changes apply straight away, with no redeploy.

image.alt: The Accounts page: cards for AI, business, Google and social connections, each with a status and Connect, Test and Edit buttons.

body.p: The page is in sections: AI (Claude, the Anthropic API, Jev, and OpenAI or ElevenLabs for voice), Business (Odoo and email inboxes), Google, Social and Settings (voice and file storage).
Each card has a status: Connected, Not set, Not connected, Error, Expires in N days, Expired (sign in again) or From Railway. Secrets are shown masked and stored encrypted on the server.

dlentry.dd: Signs in through the provider (Google, Microsoft, Meta, X, Reddit). You come back to this page with … connected as ….

dlentry.dt: Paste a token, Set up, Edit
dlentry.dd: Enter keys and settings by hand. Leave a secret blank to keep the saved one. For an IMAP mailbox, Fill in Gmail settings fills in the servers; use an app password, not your Google password.
Checks the connection now and shows the result on the card.
For a Google account: which calendars the personal assistant reads.
A value from Railway's variables is copied into the app, where you can change it; you can then delete the Railway variable.
Stops using it straight away and forgets its keys. If the same thing is set in Railway, that value is used again.

body.p: The agents run on a Claude subscription. Choose Connect on the Claude card, then Open Claude sign-in, sign in with the account whose subscription the agents should use, paste the code the page shows and choose Finish. The link works for 10 minutes. If it fails, run claude setup-token on any computer and use Paste a token.

In Social, choose Add account, pick the Platform and the business, give it a short Name the agents refer to it by (such as dms-instagram), and continue to the platform's sign-in. Add one per platform per business. Accounts are grouped by business.

Each platform's Connect button signs in through an app you register once in that platform's developer console: a Google OAuth client, a Meta app for Instagram and Threads, an X app, a Reddit app, a Microsoft app. Paste its keys here, and add the redirect address shown on the card, with Copy, to the app's allowed callbacks. If you choose Connect before the keys are in, the page asks for them first.
The redirect address needs the server's PUBLIC_BASE_URL, set in Railway.
A few settings, such as the database address and the admin token, are needed before the server can read its database, so they stay in Railway's variables. This section shows which are set.
